title: Praise to God, Immortal Praise
description: Praise to God, Immortal Praise in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 468, “Thanksgiving Hymn”, where the book credits them to Episcopal Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Praise to God, im-mor-tal praise, For the love that crowns our days! Boun-teous Source of ev-ery joy, Let Thy praise our tongues em-ploy! All to Thee, our God, we owe, Source whence all our bless-ings flow!

lines: For the love that crowns our days!
Let Thy praise our tongues employ!
All to Thee, our God, we owe,
Source whence all our blessings flow!
All the blessings of the fields,
All the stores the garden yields,
Flocks that whiten all the plain,
Lord, for these our souls shall raise
All that spring with bounteous hand
Lord, for these our souls shall raise
Lord, for these our souls shall raise

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
